article_sentences: Guwahati: The preparations for the upcoming election to the post of General Secretary of the Assam Sahitya Sabha have gathered momentum, with candidate Nayanmoni Choudhury filing his nomination papers on 11th November.
Choudhury submitted his nomination at the Sabha’s central office, Bhagawati Prasad Barua Bhawan, in Guwahati.

He arrived at the office in a convoy of around 10 vehicles, accompanied by representatives of various branches of the Assam Sahitya Sabha and literary enthusiasts from different districts across the state.
A large number of supporters and Sabha representatives from different parts of Assam were present at the venue during the nomination process.
The gathering reflected the growing activity surrounding the upcoming election, with preparations gaining pace ahead of the selection of the organisation’s next General Secretary.
The Assam Sahitya Sabha, one of the state's prominent literary organisations, plays a significant role in promoting Assamese language, literature and culture.

stories.headline: Adani Ports can absorb Evos deal costs
stories.title: Adani Ports can absorb Evos deal costs
stories.summary: New Delhi: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone will bolster the scale and diversity of its international portfolio through the proposed acquisition of Evos BV, S&P Global Ratings said Wednesday."The company can maintain its financials and credit quality after the acquisition of the liquid storage operator, in our view," the rating agency said in a statement.Also Read: Adani Ports agrees to buy Dutch storage and terminal co Evos for $2.9 bnAdani Ports and Special Economic Zone Ltd (APSEZ) last week said it has agreed to acquire 100 per cent of the Netherlands-based Evos BV from Igneo Infrastructure Partners at an enterprise value of 2.56 billion euros, marking a major expansion of its international operations and giving it a significant presence in Europe's liquid storage and energy infrastructure market."While Netherlands-headquartered Evos has limited operating synergies with Adani Ports' operations in India, the deal is consistent with the latter's growth strategy. It will allow Adani Ports to diversify its liquids portfolio with exposure to the growing market for new-age transition fuels such as sustainable aviation fuel, biofuels, methanol and bioethanol.Also Read: Adani Ports' global biz sprints, but home is still where the money is"At the same, the deal expands Adani Ports' geographic footprint into more developed markets with stable operating environments," S&P said.The all-cash transaction is valued at an enterprise value of 2.56 billion euro, equivalent to around Rs 27,000 crore, implying an equity value of approximately 1.18 billion euro. The acquisition is scheduled to be completed within 15 months, subject to regulatory approvals in India and relevant foreign jurisdictions."By our calculations, international investments could increase to about 20 per cent of the total revenue of Adani Ports from 10-15 per cent at present. We forecast the company will maintain a healthy ratio of adjusted debt to EBITDA of 2.3x in fiscal 2028 (ending March 31) and 2.7x in fiscal 2029 post the acquisition, below our downside trigger of 3.5x," S&P said.The transaction, it said, remains aligned with Adani Ports' financial policy of maintaining a net debt-to-EBITDA ratio of below 2.5x, based on the company's calculations. Potential proceeds from the company's pending stake sale in Vizhinjam port can provide a cushion to absorb growth spending over the next two years."We estimate Evos will contribute about 9 per cent of Adani Ports' total EBITDA in fiscal 2029, supporting earnings quality. Evos benefits from high average commercial occupancy of 99 per cent and stable revenue, with a substantial portion of its storage capacity being under take-or-pay contracts which are linked to consumer price index inflation," the rating agency said.Evos' robust reported EBITDA margin of 56 per cent in 2025 is similar to Adani Ports' 59 per cent in FY26.

The Cabinet also approved the continuation of credit guarantee schemes to support micro entrepreneurs, as well as women and entrepreneurs from Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

"Today, PM Narendra Modi took five major decisions in the Cabinet.
The first is the establishment of a new Yuge Yugeen Bharat National Museum, which will showcase India's cultural heritage in a very beautiful manner.
It will be the world's largest museum.
Second, the Cabinet has approved a metro rail project from Noida to Greater Noida.
Third, a fertiliser subsidy of Rs 62,370 crore has been approved for our farmers for the Rabi season.
Fourth, a credit guarantee fund of Rs 5,000 crore has been approved under the MUDRA scheme for young people aspiring to become entrepreneurs.
A credit guarantee fund of Rs 4,111 crore has also been approved under the Stand-Up India scheme for SC, ST and women entrepreneurs..." he said.
The Cabinet approved the extension of the Noida-Greater Noida Metro's Aqua Line from Noida Sector 51 to Greater Noida Sector 4 at an estimated cost of Rs 2,390 crore.
The 8.449-km corridor will have five elevated stations and is expected to be completed in four years.

stories.headline: Tamil Nadu may approach Supreme Court seeking greater powers for Cauvery Water Management Authority
stories.title: Tamil Nadu may approach Supreme Court seeking greater powers for Cauvery Water Management Authority
stories.summary: The State wants the Authority to be modelled along the lines of the Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB)
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Frustrated that the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) does not have the power to enforce its orders, Tamil Nadu is contemplating approaching the Supreme Court with a prayer that the Authority be given teeth.
It wants the Authority to be modelled along the lines of the Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB), a case of which has been mentioned in the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal’s report (Volume V).

Established in October 1967, the BBMB is engaged in the regulation of the supply of water and electricity from Bhakra Nangal and Beas projects to Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Himachal Pradesh, Delhi, and Chandigarh.

The CWMA chairperson Saumitra Kumar Haldar, too, in an interaction with The Hindu in August, referred to the Tribunal’s recommendation and explained that the Board, with the chief being appointed by the Union government, “owns, operates, manages, and regulates” the projects.
“They [the BBMB] take joint decisions regarding how much water is to be given and what the scheduling will be.
Everything is planned,” Mr. Haldar had said.

Tamil Nadu has been complaining that despite the quantities of water release stipulated by the CWMA in the last three-odd months being inadequate and lower than the proportionate share, the upper riparian State of Karnataka has not provided water, as per the mandated releases.

Of the seven spells of the 15-day water release ordered by the Authority since July 29, Karnataka has not complied with the release in five spells, even though, cumulatively, Tamil Nadu realised about 5,000 cubic feet per second (cusecs) higher than the total figure of 5.71 lakh cusecs, according to a persual of the data measured at Biligundulu on the inter-State border of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

As per the data available with the Central Water Commission, four reservoirs of Karnataka (Krishnaraja Sagara, Kabini, Hemavathi, and Harangi) registered a net cumulative inflow of about 132 thousand million cubic feet (tmc ft) during the period of June 1 to November 4, marking a shortfall of around 54%.
The 30-year-long average net inflow was around 288 tmc ft.

If the same shortfall is to be applied in the case of Tamil Nadu, the realisation should have been around 67 tmc ft between June 1 and November 4 against the quantum of approximately 145 tmc ft in a normal year.
But Biligundulu received 53.43 tmc ft only with a shortfall of around 13 tmc ft.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Monthly Roundup: September 2026
stories.title: Supreme Court Monthly Roundup: September 2026
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Case Details: Anil Singh @ Anil Kumar Singh.
State of Bihar & Ors.

The Supreme Court cautioned the trial courts to proceed with alacrity during trial, especially when there is a total failure of the prosecution for not conducting examination of the crucial witnesses.
“…when there is total failure of the prosecution, the Court should with alacrity question the prosecution's conduct in not examining crucial witnesses.

The Trial Court is not a moot spectator and even in the role of an unbiased adjudicator has the responsibility to ensure that the best evidence is not suppressed by the prosecution…”, observed a bench of Justice J.B. Pardiwala and Justice K. Vinod Chandran, while setting aside the concurrent findings of the Patna High Court and Trial Court's order rejecting the de-facto complainant Section 311 Cr.P.C. application seeking examination of the crucial witness which could have a direct impact on the outcome of the trial.
The case arose from an altercation in which the appellant and his father sustained injuries.
Case Details: Ummed Devi.
State of Rajasthan and Anr.
The Supreme Court has disapproved of dismissing appeals on technical grounds like the absence of a delay condonation application when the litigant was not having proper legal assistance.
It is the duty of the Courts to ensure quality legal assistance to the litigants.

“True that the appeal should have been accompanied with an application for condonation of delay, but the Constitutional Courts should also be alive to the travails of a litigant and if the legal assistance is not adequate, it has a duty to provide quality legal assistance to the litigants, whether it be a victim or an accused.”, observed a bench of Justice J.B. Pardiwala and Justice K. Vinod Chandran, while setting aside the Rajasthan High Court's decision which had dismissed the appeal against an acquittal in a dowry death case merely for want of an application seeking condonation of delay with an appeal.
The victim's mother filed the appeal against the accused's acquittal before the High Court with a 19-day delay.

stories.headline: Savitribai Phule Pune University Floats Tender for 1 MWp Rooftop Solar With 5 MWh BESS
stories.title: Savitribai Phule Pune University Floats Tender for 1 MWp Rooftop Solar With 5 MWh BESS
stories.summary: Savitribai Phule Pune University (SPPU), Maharashtra, has invited bids for installing a 1 MWp rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) system integrated with a 5 MWh battery energy storage system ( BESS ) across various buildings on its campus. The project will be implemented under the Renewable Energy Service Company (RESCO) model. The tender was published on November 6, 2026. Bids can be submitted until November 30, 2026, at 3 PM, with the opening scheduled for December 1. According to the tender, the scope includes the supply, erection, testing and commissioning of the rooftop-mounted solar PV system and battery storage infrastructure. The project comprises 1,000 kWp of solar capacity and 5,000 kWh of battery storage. 25-year RESCO arrangement Under the RESCO model, the developer is responsible for installing and operating the renewable energy system, while the consumer purchases the electricity generated under an agreed commercial arrangement. The tender specifies a 25-year period for electricity generation and supply from the rooftop solar and BESS project. This arrangement allows the university to procure renewable electricity without necessarily undertaking the entire upfront capital investment for the installation. The tender's bill of quantities (BOQ) also lists a rate of ₹32 per kWh for electricity generated and supplied through the project over the 25-year period. This is a quoted BOQ rate and should not be confused with a final awarded tariff. Eligibility and bidding requirements The university has specified technical qualification requirements for prospective bidders. These include experience in executing a single similar project of at least 1,500 kWp during the last five financial years, along with cumulative project execution experience of at least 3,000 kWp during the same period. Bidders must also demonstrate experience in installing at least one battery energy storage system with a capacity of 500 kWh. The tender carries an earnest money deposit (EMD) of ₹10 lakh and a tender fee of ₹10,000. The bid validity period is 120 days. Universities expand campus solar installations SPPU's proposed project comes amid wider solar adoption across India's higher education institutions, with universities and IITs increasingly using campus rooftops and available land to generate electricity and reduce dependence on grid power. IIT Roorkee, for instance, has reported a cumulative rooftop solar capacity of 2.8 MWp, including a 1 MWp plant installed under the RESCO model. Its solar installations cover 27 departmental and institutional buildings. Similarly, IIT Kanpur's Sustainability Report 2024-25 puts its existing solar generation capacity at 2.21 MW, comprising 1 MW under the CAPEX model and 1.21 MW under RESCO. The institute is also installing an additional 0.4 MW system and has assessed the potential to expand its solar capacity to 10 MW. IIT Guwahati signed an agreement with ICICI Foundation in February 2026 to establish a 2 MW solar power plant on its campus. Meanwhile, IIM Bangalore's rooftop solar installation is expected to meet approximately 15% of the institute's electricity requirements. The trend extends beyond the IIT system. Jindal Global University reported 2.4 MW of on-site solar capacity and generated 25.56 lakh kWh of solar electricity in 2025, more than double its 2024 generation of 11.82 lakh kWh. For SPPU, integrating a 5 MWh BESS with rooftop solar introduces another dimension to campus energy management. While solar installations help institutions generate electricity locally, battery storage can shift some of that generation to periods when sunlight is unavailable. However, the project's eventual contribution will depend on its battery power rating, operating schedule, energy procurement arrangement and actual utilisation. Its implementation could offer a useful reference for other large institutional consumers considering solar-plus-storage installations.

reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Indian customs is holding dozens of containers of bulk Scotch imported by Pernod Ricard and Diageo as investigators press for a 150 per cent tariff, even though the companies rely on a New Delhi assurance of lower duties under the India-UK trade pact, according to four people with knowledge of the matter and a confidential government memo.

In the first major dispute linked to the trade deal, which took effect in July, customs investigators have ordered the higher tariff on the shipments arguing that bulk Scotch concentrates used to make whisky brands are not eligible for the pact’s reduced 75 per cent duty.
The investigators say the lower rate applies only to finished products such as bottled, ready-to-drink Scotch.

Following industry lobbying, India’s commerce ministry assured senior executives on November 2, 2026 that it would honour the pact and resolve the dispute as soon as possible, leading liquor companies to believe the lower tariff would be applied.

However, a memo by the finance ministry’s Directorate of Revenue Intelligence dated November 4, 2026, reviewed by Reuters, asks customs commissioners across India to continue to take a different view.

The memo said importers were “incorrectly” claiming benefits under the India-UK pact on bulk Scotch, which should attract a 150 per cent tariff under a customs classification in effect since May 1 for so-called “compound alcoholic preparations”.

Any misclassification by importers has “large-scale, recurring substantial revenue implications”, the memo said, instructing customs officials to ensure the correct application of the 150 per cent duty.

“Preliminary investigation revealed that the imported goods are not finished whisky/brand/rum as such, but are concentrates/compound preparations which are subjected to further manufacturing,” the confidential memo said, providing the clearest explanation yet of investigators’ position.
India’s finance ministry, which oversees customs authorities, and the commerce ministry did not respond to Reuters queries.
The revenue directorate also did not respond.
The finance ministry and commerce ministry “are under discussion for an appropriate resolution of the matter”, a senior finance ministry source said.
Pernod, which owns UK-based Scotch whisky producer Chivas Brothers, and Diageo did not reply to requests for comment.

stories.headline: India's GDP growth to beat RBI forecast? SBI sees 7.8% expansion in Q2; Moody's raises FY27 outlook
stories.title: India's GDP growth to beat RBI forecast? SBI sees 7.8% expansion in Q2; Moody's raises FY27 outlook
stories.summary: According to SBI Research, India's economic activity remained robust during July–September 2026, supported by manufacturing, services, corporate profitability and accelerating bank credit.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The research team used a dynamic factor model incorporating 54 high-frequency indicators to estimate second-quarter growth.
What is driving India's growth?
SBI Research noted that approximately 88% of 50 leading economic indicators showed acceleration in Q2 FY27, compared with 86% in the preceding quarter.
Manufacturing growth is projected at 8.7%, while services are expected to expand 9.7%, highlighting the continued strength of industrial and services activity.
Gross Value Added (GVA), which measures economic output across sectors, could grow between 8% and 8.2%.
Corporate earnings also indicate improving business conditions.
EBITDA and profit after tax of approximately 2,300 listed companies, excluding banking and financial services, increased 35% and 33%, respectively, year-on-year.
Bank lending remained another important growth driver.
Scheduled commercial bank credit growth accelerated to 18.2%, while deposit growth reached 16.7% for the fortnight ended October 15.
SBI Research also expects nominal GDP growth of 11–11.5% in the September quarter.
Separately, Moody's Ratings upgraded India's FY27 economic growth projection to 7% from its earlier estimate of 6.5%.

"India's broad-based economic momentum and demonstrated resilience to the energy supply shock warrant upward revisions to our 2026-27 growth forecasts to 7 per cent from 6.5 per cent," Moody's said in its Global Macro Outlook 2027–28.
